Read, write, and convert graphs between graph-tool (.gt) and igraph

graph_io.Rd

Native C++ reader and writer for the graph-tool binary .gt file format (version 1, both little-endian and big-endian, with optional gzip/bzip2/xz/zstd compression) and lossless bidirectional conversion with igraph graph objects.

Usage

read_gt(file)
write_gt(graph, file, comment = NULL,
         compression = c("auto", "none", "gzip", "bzip2", "xz", "zstd"))
graph_load(file, fmt = c("auto", "gt", "graphml", "gml", "edgelist"), ...)
graph_save(graph, file, fmt = c("auto", "gt", "graphml", "gml", "edgelist"), ...)
as_igraph(graph, include_properties = TRUE)
from_igraph(graph, include_properties = TRUE)

Arguments

file

Path to the input or output graph file.

graph

An rgraphtool_graph object (for write_gt(), graph_save(), and as_igraph()) or an igraph object (for from_igraph()).

comment

Optional single character string stored in the .gt header comment field. When NULL, a descriptive default header is generated.

compression

Compression applied when writing .gt files. "auto" infers compression from the file extension (.gz, .bz2, .xz, .zst); read_gt() automatically detects compression from magic bytes.

fmt

File format for graph_load() and graph_save(). "auto" infers the format from the file extension. "gt" uses the native C++ binary reader/writer without external dependencies; "graphml", "gml", and "edgelist" delegate to igraph.

include_properties

Logical; whether to transfer graph, vertex, and edge property maps during igraph conversion.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to write_gt() (for fmt = "gt") or to igraph::read_graph() / igraph::write_graph().

Details

read_gt() and write_gt() implement the official graph-tool binary .gt specification directly in C++ with no Python dependency. They preserve directedness, parallel edges, self-loops, isolated vertices, and all 15 graph-tool internal property map types (bool, int16_t, int32_t, int64_t, double, long double, string, their vector<T> counterparts, and raw pickled python::object payloads) across graph, vertex, and edge property maps. Numeric edge properties loaded from .gt or imported via from_igraph() are stored directly in C++ so weighted and layered SBM inference functions and C++ extensions can access them immediately.

as_igraph() and from_igraph() require the optional igraph package and preserve vertex counts, directedness, parallel edges, self-loops, and graph, vertex, and edge attributes.

Value

read_gt(), graph_load(), and from_igraph() return an rgraphtool_graph object. as_igraph() returns an igraph object. write_gt() and graph_save() invisibly return file.

Examples

g <- graph_create(4L, directed = TRUE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 1), c(2, 4)),
                properties = list(weight = c(1.2, 0.8, 2.5, 1.0)))
graph_set_vertex_property(g, "name", c("a", "b", "c", "d"))
graph_set_graph_property(g, "title", "example")

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".gt.gz")
write_gt(g, f)
g2 <- read_gt(f)
graph_edge_property(g2, "weight")
#> [1] 1.2 0.8 1.0 2.5
graph_vertex_property(g2, "name")
#> [1] "a" "b" "c" "d"
unlink(f)

if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ig <- as_igraph(g)
  g3 <- from_igraph(ig)
  graph_num_edges(g3)
}
#> [1] 4
